In many contexts, this term is used to describe tribes or clans, emphasizing the importance of communal bonds and relationships in Islamic societies.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Islamic context, the term "Qabila" has deep spiritual significance. It relates to the "People of the House," specifically referring to the Prophet Muhammad and his family. This group is considered an esteemed and privileged Qabila in Islamic tradition, bound by a sacred duty to protect, preserve, and uphold the Prophet's teachings and the noble virtues of his household. Furthermore, all Muslims are considered part of the broader Islamic Qabila, bound together by their common faith, obligations to God, and adherence to the Prophet's teachings and practices.
